Synopsis:
    Oscar-winning director Laura Poitras and co-director Rachel Lauren Mueller premiered a 25-minute documentary at the Venice Film Festival chronicling ICE deportation raids in Minneapolis. The film documents community volunteer networks tracking ICE movements, confrontations between agents and protesters (including two U.S. citizens shot dead), and a Mexican man evading authorities. Directors frame the film as a counter-narrative to media normalization of immigration enforcement violence. The Minneapolis operation was eventually scaled back, with ICE reportedly withdrawing 80% of its agents, which filmmakers attribute to sustained community resistance.
